**Proposed mechanism:** ABCA1 (HGNC:7) —DISRUPTS→ cholesterol efflux (GO:0006874); APOA1 (HGNC:780) —DISRUPTS→ cholesterol efflux (GO:0006874); cholesterol efflux (GO:0006874) —LEADS_TO→ HDL metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-174272); HDL metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-174272) —DECREASES→ low HDL cholesterol (HP:0011011); HDL metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-174272) —INCREASES→ atherosclerosis (HP:0002616); HDL metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-174272) —INCREASES→ enlarged tonsils (HP:0011731). Loss-of-function mutations in ABCA1 disrupt the efflux of cholesterol from cells to APOA1. This impaired cholesterol efflux leads to defective HDL metabolism, resulting in low HDL cholesterol levels and an increased risk of atherosclerosis. In Tangier disease, this also manifests with enlarged tonsils due to accumulation of lipid-laden foam cells.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of a common pathogenic variant in ABCA1 or APOA1 with a population frequency greater than 1% in gnomAD would challenge the causal role of these genes in either disease. _(variant: rs2004640)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared ABCA1/APOA1 pathway defect in these conditions highlights the critical role of cholesterol efflux and HDL metabolism in cardiovascular health. Therapeutic strategies aimed at enhancing ABCA1 activity or APOA1 levels could potentially benefit patients with both Tangier disease and hypoalphalipoproteinemia type 2.
